summary: Frontend-only retest of the footer z-index fix on the MBtex Group landing page. Verified on mobile (390x844) and desktop (1920x800) that the scroll-lines layer is no longer visible inside the footer, that lines remain visible/animating in other sections, and that footer nav links still scroll correctly with zero console errors. All checks PASSED.
critical_code_review_comments: Non-blocking console warning present on load (pre-existing, both viewports): framer-motion useScroll logs 'Please ensure that the container has a non-static position, like relative/fixed/absolute to ensure scroll offset is calculated correctly.' Likely a useScroll({target/container}) usage in a section component whose container is static. Cosmetic only, but worth cleaning up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Footer z-index bug (scroll lines visible through footer) is FIXED and verified. Programmatic verification technique used: set [data-testid='scroll-lines'] style.pointerEvents='auto' + all child paths pointerEvents='stroke', then elementFromPoint on an 8x6 grid inside the footer rect; 0 hits belonged to the lines layer on both 390x844 and 1920x800. Measured: footer computed position=relative, z-index=10, bg=rgb(7,26,51); lines layer z-index=5, pointer-events=none. Lines layer transform changes on scroll on both viewports (mobile -650 -> -900; desktop -1300 -> -2200), so the fix did not hide lines globally. Footer nav links all scroll their target section to top=60px (header offset) — must wait ~2s after click because Lenis smooth scroll is in flight (measuring too early gives misleading offsets). Contact form/tabs not retested per request (covered in iterations 4-5).
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: <footer> was position:static, so its opaque navy background could not create a stacking context above the fixed ScrollLines layer (z-5), letting the lines paint over the footer background. Fix ('relative z-10' on the footer) is correct and confirmed effective; lines are now clipped exactly at the footer top border.
